title: Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) Report - Ransomware Landscape in Africa 2024

1. executive_summary.content: In 2024, AFRINTEL documented 86 African victims publicly associated with ransomware or data-extortion activity. The activity affected 24 countries, with a strong concentration in South Africa (30 victims, 34.9%), followed by Egypt, Tunisia, Namibia, and several West/East African economies. The second half of the year was more active (55 victims, compared with 31 in the first half).
key_findings: LockBit3: most active group with 16 victims (18.6%)

2. methodology.content: The report was rebuilt from the verified AFRINTEL 2024 victim list containing exactly 86 entries, each normalized by country, region, ransomware group, month of publication, sector, public domain, and description. Sector statistics are grouped into macro-sectors to avoid misleading fragmentation.
limitations: Data covering only public claims and public leak-site visibility.
Some victim descriptions remain limited when public business context is scarce.
Attribution based on the actor name associated with the public listing, not forensically confirmed.

3. country_distribution.analytical_reading: South Africa alone represents almost one third of the 2024 dataset. This is consistent with its large digital economy, dense enterprise ecosystem, mature financial sector and high public visibility of ransomware claims.

4. industry_sector_distribution.analytical_reading: Financial services, insurance, banking and fintech-related entities form the most exposed macro-sector, reflecting the value of financial data and the pressure ransomware actors can apply. Technology and IT services are also highly represented, creating a potential supply-chain risk.

5. ransomware_groups_activity.analytical_reading: LockBit3 remains the most visible actor in the AFRINTEL 2024 dataset, despite global disruption efforts. RansomHub appears as a major extortion actor with broad targeting. The long tail of smaller groups confirms the fragmentation of the ransomware/extortion ecosystem.

6. geostrategic_regional_analysis.interpretation: Southern Africa is the main ransomware/exposure zone in 2024 (driven by South Africa, Namibia, Zimbabwe). North Africa follows, with Egypt as the main driver. Central Africa remains underrepresented in open-source ransomware visibility.

7. monthly_timeline_and_trends.trend_assessment: The second half of 2024 shows a clear increase in public ransomware/extortion visibility. This pattern suggests that African organizations should strengthen monitoring before holiday periods and month-end/quarter-end business cycles.

9. strategic_recommendations: Backup resilience: Apply the 3-2-1 rule, keep offline/immutable backups.
Identity security: Enforce MFA on VPN, RDP, cloud admin portals, email and privileged accounts.
Exposure management: Continuously audit exposed services and vulnerable applications.
Network segmentation: Separate critical servers, OT/ICS networks, backup infrastructure and admin workstations.
SOC correlation: Correlate authentication anomalies, endpoint discovery, archive creation and outbound data transfer.
Incident response: Maintain a ransomware playbook with legal, communications, technical and executive decision paths.
CTI monitoring: Track actor claims, but avoid overreliance on IoCs; prioritize TTP-based detection and sector exposure.
Ransom payment: Not recommended. It does not guarantee data recovery or non-disclosure and can fund further criminal activity.
sections.10. conclusion: The 2024 AFRINTEL dataset confirms that ransomware and data-extortion actors are consistently targeting African organizations across public, private and critical sectors. The threat is not limited to a single region or industry. For 2025 and beyond, African SOC teams should prioritize identity hardening, exposed-service reduction, backup resilience, data-exfiltration detection and regional CTI sharing.
